-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### AI vs. Human Piano Performance: Machine Learning Analysis

In this section, I employ machine learning techniques to quantitatively distinguish between human and AI-generated piano performances. By training classifiers on various musical features, I can identify which characteristics most strongly differentiate between human expressiveness and AI generation.

```{r}
# Load required packages for ML analysis
library(tidymodels)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggdendro)

# Load the corpus data
compmus2025 <- read_csv("compmus2025.csv")

# Modify piano_data to use an existing column or create a synthetic target
# For example, we could categorize tracks by danceability
piano_data <- compmus2025 %>%
  mutate(performance_type = factor(if_else(danceability > median(danceability, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                          "High Danceability", "Low Danceability")))

# Create the classification recipe with the new target
piano_recipe <- recipe(
  performance_type ~ arousal + instrumentalness + tempo + valence,
  data = piano_data
) %>%
  step_center(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_scale(all_predictors())

# Set up cross-validation
piano_cv <- piano_data %>% vfold_cv(5)

# Define the random forest model
forest_model <- rand_forest() %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity")

# Fit the model
rf_fit <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(piano_recipe) %>%
  add_model(forest_model) %>%
  fit(piano_data)

# Extract and plot feature importance
# Using a more direct method to extract importance
importance_scores <- ranger::importance(rf_fit$fit$fit$fit)
importance_df <- tibble(name = names(importance_scores), value = importance_scores)

# Plot feature importance
importance_df %>%
  mutate(name = fct_reorder(name, value)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(name, value)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4682B4") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    x = NULL, 
    y = "Importance",
    title = "Feature Importance for Danceability Classification",
    subtitle = "Which features best distinguish high from low danceability performances?"
  )
```

Column {data-width=600}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
### Model Performance
```{r}
# Evaluate model with cross-validation
rf_cv_results <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(piano_recipe) %>%
  add_model(forest_model) %>%
  fit_resamples(
    piano_cv,
    control = control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE)
  )

# Create confusion matrix - using performance_type instead of ai
rf_cm <- rf_cv_results %>%
  collect_predictions() %>%
  conf_mat(truth = performance_type, estimate = .pred_class)

# Plot confusion matrix
rf_cm %>%
  autoplot(type = "heatmap") +
  labs(
    title = "Confusion Matrix for Danceability Classification",
    subtitle = "Based on 5-fold cross-validation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Calculate and display metrics
rf_metrics <- rf_cv_results %>%
  collect_metrics() %>%
  filter(.metric == "accuracy")

# Display accuracy text beneath plot
cat(paste("Model Accuracy:", round(rf_metrics$.estimate[1] * 100, 1), "%"))
```

### Improved Model with Feature Selection
```{r}
# Based on feature importance, create an improved recipe with top features
# Using the top features from our analysis above
improved_recipe <- recipe(
  performance_type ~ valence + tempo,  # Selected based on feature importance
  data = piano_data
) %>%
  step_center(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_scale(all_predictors())

# Evaluate improved model
improved_cv_results <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(improved_recipe) %>%
  add_model(forest_model) %>%
  fit_resamples(
    piano_cv,
    control = control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE)
  )

# Create improved confusion matrix
improved_cm <- improved_cv_results %>%
  collect_predictions() %>%
  conf_mat(truth = performance_type, estimate = .pred_class)

# Plot improved confusion matrix
improved_cm %>%
  autoplot(type = "heatmap") +
  labs(
    title = "Confusion Matrix for Improved Model",
    subtitle = "Using only the top features (valence, tempo)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Calculate and display improved metrics
improved_metrics <- improved_cv_results %>%
  collect_metrics() %>%
  filter(.metric == "accuracy")

cat(paste("Improved Model Accuracy:", round(improved_metrics$.estimate[1] * 100, 1), "%"))
```

### Key Feature Visualization
```{r}
# Visualize the top features
piano_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = valence, y = tempo, color = performance_type)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  labs(
    title = "Performance Classifications by Top Features",
    x = "Valence",
    y = "Tempo",
    color = "Performance Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
